name: Beauty-Horror Tonal Contrast
use_when: A serious or horrific sequence needs a haunting, bitter, or sickening contrast rather than straightforward dread.
The imagery has an unsettling beauty or formal elegance that can be ethically complicated by the right track.
The editor wants viewers to feel discomfort, grief, critique, or historical irony.
avoid_when: The contrast would glorify harm, violence, disaster, war, crisis, or death.
The subject involves real victims and the user has not approved a stylized approach.
The music makes the scene feel cool, triumphant, or entertaining instead of disturbing.
A restrained documentary score or natural sound would preserve dignity better.

timeline_pattern.pattern: serious_context -> beautiful_or_nostalgic_track -> horrific_image -> discomfort_registers -> ethical_story_check -> keep_or_reject
timeline_pattern.contrast_rule: The beauty of the track should sharpen the horror through irony or grief, not soften it.
timeline_pattern.rejection_rule: A music experiment can be artistically interesting and still wrong for the final story.
timeline_pattern.approval_rule: For sensitive material, prefer restraint unless the contrast has a clear ethical purpose.

motion.rule: Avoid flashy motion that combines with beautiful music to make harm look glamorous.

sound.rule: Use beautiful, nostalgic, or lyrical music only when it creates haunting tension and passes an ethical tone check.
sound.mix: Keep any necessary narration or warning context intelligible so the contrast is not misread.

captions.rule: Use captions or title context when needed to prevent the contrast from being misunderstood as celebration.

color.rule: Do not pair beauty-horror music with a grade that glamorizes damage or hides evidence.

implementation.ffmpeg: Render an A/B comparison between restrained scoring and contrast scoring. Review levels so the music does not overwhelm necessary context or warnings.
implementation.remotion: Store sensitive contrast choices with fields for ethicalPurpose, intendedEmotion, risk, approvalStatus, and rejectReason.
implementation.blender: Keep animated treatment restrained; avoid celebratory movement over real harm unless explicitly approved as satire or critique.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Test the contrast version beside a restrained version and choose the one that preserves dignity and story clarity.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers for context, contrast entry, disturbing image, narration/warning, and ethical review.

common_mistakes: Using a beautiful track because it feels cinematic while ignoring the subject's dignity.
Letting contrast turn horror into spectacle.
Keeping an experiment because it is interesting even after it feels ethically too far.
Removing context that tells the viewer how to read the contrast.
Assuming all serious topics need grim music when a controlled contrast may be more haunting.
qc: Does the contrast create discomfort, grief, critique, or irony rather than glamour?
Would a viewer reasonably think the edit is celebrating the harm?
Is a restrained version tested for comparison?
Is the track rejected if it is interesting but too far for the subject?
